core_obligations: Assume (1) and let Z -> Y be arbitrary; choose a surjective etale V -> Y with V a scheme (proof lines 1529-1531).
Write down the square of topological spaces and record that its horizontal arrows are open and surjective and that the comparison map is surjective (proof lines 1532-1543).
Conclude that |Z x_Y X| -> |Z| is closed, which is (2), and note that (2) implies (1) by definition (proof lines 1544-1547).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a representable morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, universal closedness in the representable sense is equivalent to |Z x_Y X| -> |Z| being closed for every morphism Z -> Y (source lines 1516-1526). The proof is the same topological square argument as for submersiveness: choose a surjective etale V -> Y, use that V x_Y X -> V is universally closed as a morphism of schemes, and observe that in the square comparing |V x_Y X| -> |V| with |Z x_Y X| -> |Z| the horizontal arrows are open and surjective and the comparison map |V x_Y X| -> |V| x_{|Z|} |Z x_Y X| is surjective, so closedness of the left vertical arrow forces closedness of the right one; the converse is immediate.
